decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line in the firm's main market, uncertainty after only one year is still high and the learning value likely exceeds the cost of keeping it available.
A comfort insole is a low-cost complement to the footwear range, so management would usually keep the option open longer unless sales data clearly disappoint.
The supportive insole fits the firm's protective-footwear ecosystem and is relatively inexpensive to maintain, though overlap with other insoles raises some pruning risk later.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series is strategically aligned with workplace innovation and its dedicated page suggests stronger commitment, so it is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon.
Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized niche with higher complexity and likely higher carrying costs, but the firm would still usually allow more time before abandoning the option.
A moulded insole shown on the home page appears to have strategic emphasis and can be retained at relatively low incremental cost while demand becomes clearer.
